title: Chapter 6 Quiz: Component Communication Deep Dive
description: Test your knowledge of advanced communication techniques: props, events, v-model, provide/inject, scoped slots, and best practices.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `emits` option in a Vue component?
options: To define the events the component listens to
To document and optionally validate the custom events the component can emit
To define the props the component accepts
questions.explanation: The `emits` option declares the custom events a component can emit, with optional validation.

questions.question: When using `v-model` on a custom component in Vue 3, the component must accept a `value` prop and emit an `input` event.
questions.explanation: In Vue 3, the default is `modelValue` prop and `update:modelValue` event. The `value`/`input` convention was used in Vue 2.

questions.question: To create a custom component that supports a `v-model:title` binding, the component should accept a `title` prop and emit an event named __________.
questions.explanation: For a `v-model` with an argument, the corresponding event name is `update:argument`.

questions.question: Provide/Inject is designed to replace Vuex/Pinia for global state management.
questions.explanation: Provide/Inject is not intended for global state; it's for avoiding prop drilling. Use Pinia for global app state.

questions.question: What is a scoped slot?
options: A slot that is only available in development mode
A slot that allows the child component to pass data to the parent's slot template
A slot that is automatically named
A slot that can be used only once
questions.explanation: Scoped slots let the child pass data to the parent's slot content, enabling custom rendering of each item.

questions.question: To avoid prop drilling, you can use __________ to provide data from an ancestor to any descendant.
questions.explanation: Provide/Inject is the built‑in solution for dependency injection, allowing ancestors to make data available to deep descendants.

questions.question: What is the recommended way for two sibling components to communicate?
options: Lift shared state to a common parent and use props/events
questions.explanation: The standard pattern is to lift state up to the closest common ancestor and communicate through props and events.

questions.question: A component can both provide and inject data.
questions.explanation: Yes, a component can be a provider for its descendants and also inject from its ancestors.

questions.question: To make a provided value reactive, you can provide a __________ or a computed property.
questions.explanation: If you provide a plain value, changes won't propagate. Provide a ref to make it reactive.

questions.question: Which of the following is an anti‑pattern in component communication?
options: Using props to pass data down
Using events to notify parent of changes
Using `$parent` to directly call a method on the parent
Using scoped slots for list rendering
questions.explanation: Accessing `$parent` creates tight coupling and is hard to maintain. Use props and events instead.

questions.question: You can combine multiple `v-model` bindings on the same component, like `v-model:first-name` and `v-model:last-name`.
questions.explanation: Yes, Vue 3 supports multiple `v-model` bindings with different arguments.

questions.question: When using scoped slots, the child component binds data to the slot using the __________ attribute.
questions.explanation: You use `v-bind` or `:` on the `<slot>` element to pass props to the slot scope.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `validator` function in a prop definition?
options: To run custom validation logic on the prop value
questions.explanation: The `validator` function allows custom validation beyond type checking, returning `true` if valid.

questions.question: In a component that uses `provide`, the provided value is automatically reactive if it is a primitive.
questions.explanation: Primitives are not reactive. To make provided values reactive, you must provide a ref, reactive object, or computed property.

questions.question: Which pattern is best for a highly reusable list component that needs to let the parent customize each item's rendering?
options: Using a prop to pass a render function
questions.explanation: Scoped slots give the parent full control over how each item is rendered, keeping the list component generic.

questions.question: The shorthand for `v-slot:default` is __________.
questions.explanation: The `#` shorthand works for any slot name, including `#default` for the unnamed slot.

questions.question: A component can emit multiple events with the same name, and they will be queued and handled sequentially.
questions.explanation: Yes, `$emit` triggers all listeners attached to that event, and they execute synchronously.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using `v-model` on a component?
options: It reduces code by replacing props and events with a single directive
It makes the component more performant
It allows two‑way binding in a declarative way
questions.explanation: `v-model` provides a concise, declarative syntax for two‑way binding between a parent and a child component.

questions.question: To access the slot props in a scoped slot, you use the __________ directive with a destructuring pattern.
questions.explanation: The `v-slot` directive (or its shorthand `#`) is used to receive slot props.

questions.question: You can use provide/inject to pass functions, allowing descendants to call methods on the ancestor.
questions.explanation: Yes, providing a function is a common pattern to allow children to trigger actions in an ancestor.
